svg.title: Anchor and grout detail
svg.text: (a) Post-installed bonded anchor M24 + epoxy grout (scale 1:4 on A3, mm)
nut + washer: torque from the ETA (example 250 N·m),
only after the grout has cured
jack bolt M20 on a small steel plate: levels the machine,
then backed off after the grout has cured (load → grout)
beyond the plate, 45° chamfer, no voids under the plate
formwork tight, waxed / foil, poured from ONE side
concrete chipped to sound aggregate, roughness ≥ 3 mm,
threaded rod M24 8.8 + injection mortar (epoxy, with ETA),
hole Ø28 × 200 (h_ef = 200), cleaned 2× blow – brush – blow
c = 150 mm ≥ 1.5·h_ef = 300 mm is NOT met → the concrete cone is
reduced: N_Rd,c = 72.6 → 46.3 kN (§C5.3); check with the ETA software
(b) Cast-in anchor in a sleeve + cementitious grout
head box: a grout head of 100–150 above the plate bottom
pushes the grout under the plate (pour from one side only)
steel shim pack / wedge next to each bolt (or a levelling bolt)
concrete pre-wetted 24 h, saturated surface dry (no puddles)
corrugated sleeve Ø80 × 200: the bolt can move ±5 mm for the
final position; the sleeve is grouted after levelling
anchor bolt M24 cast in with a steel template (±5 mm)
Epoxy vs cementitious grout (typical class values – the datasheet decides)
F = T / (K·d) K = nut factor: 0.20 dry, 0.15 oiled, 0.10–0.12 MoS₂
stress: 52 083 N / 353 mm² = 147.5 MPa = 23 % of f_y (8.8: 640 MPa)
VDI 2230, μ = 0.12: F = 64.5 kN (K_eq = 0.161) – friction decides!
Steel N_Rd,s = 188.3 kN (EN 1992-4) – the concrete cone governs.
EXAMPLE – check the maker's installation manual
